decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location Plan2105	Proposed Fourth Floor Plan2016	Proposed Roof Plan2113 Proposed South-West Elevation2111 Proposed South-East Elevation2110 Proposed North-West Elevation2112 Proposed North-East Elevation2116 Proposed Section B-B2115 Proposed Section A-A2117 Proposed Section C-CReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture those specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area

Prior to occupation, waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the permitted number of occupiers shall be provided on site, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities are to be retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. No existing parking spaces shall be extinguished for the purposes of compliance with this condition.  Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets

Prior to occupation, seven long-stay cycle parking spaces shall be provided and unless otherwise agreed cycle parking should be provided in compliance with the following criteria:o	in an accessible location: the access route to the store should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike too	enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door) whicho	must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2mo	secured: with a British Standard mortice lock or access fobo	fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roofThe approved bicycle parking shall be provided prior to occupation and thereafter permanently retained. No existing parking spaces shall be extinguished for the purposes of compliance with this condition. Reason: To ensure that sufficient provision at all times so that the development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or the conditions of general safety along the adjacent highway, or the amenities and convenience of existing local residents.

No development shall commence until a Site-Specific Flood Risk and Surface Water Verification Scheme has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include:1.	A topographical survey of the site and the primary access and egress route(s) to an area of Flood Zone 1.2.	Hydraulic modelling and Hazard Mapping demonstrating that a 'Low Hazard' route (as defined in Table 13.1 of FD2320/TR2) is maintained during a 1-in-100 year plus climate change flood event, accounting for combined fluvial and surface water flood risks.3.	Detailed Surface Water Drainage Strategy (SuDS): Evidence that the new storey will not increase surface water runoff rates. This shall include details of any attenuation measures (e.g. blue/green roofs or rainwater harvesting) to ensure runoff is managed in accordance with the September 2025 PPG update.4.	A Flood Warning and Evacuation Plan (FWEP) including a permanent safe refuge within the new storey.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved scheme and maintained as such thereafter. Reason: To ensure the safety of future occupants and to ensure the development does not increase flood risk elsewhere, in accordance with the NPPF, the September 2025 PPG update, and the requirements of Schedule 2, Part 20, Class A of the GPDO. This is required prior to commencement as the host building is located within a surface water flood risk area and the impact of the additional storey must be mitigated before works begin
